segments.source: Mina is 15 years old. A library rule says: a child may enter the archive room if age ≥ 12 AND an adult permit is present. Exception: during an evacuation drill, nobody may enter. Permit present: yes. Evacuation drill: yes.
Rules.
Check exceptions first if they override the general rule. Otherwise every condition joined by AND must be true.
Task.
May Mina enter the archive room under these facts? Show which conditions succeed or fail.
Step-by-step solution.
1. The evacuation exception applies and overrides ordinary eligibility. 2. Therefore entry is not allowed.
Answer.
No, Mina may not enter.
Knowledge takeaway.
The order of reasoning matters when exceptions override ordinary rules.
Formal model.
Boolean rule with priority: exception predicate first, then conjunction of eligibility conditions.
C2. Rights as limits on decisions
Problem 346. Majority rule and a protected right: case 1
Knowledge context.
Democratic procedures use voting, but constitutional systems can place some rights beyond ordinary majority power.
Given facts.

A council of 19 members votes 14 to 5 for a proposal that would forbid one named group from the right to speak at a peaceful meeting. The classroom constitution states: (1) ordinary proposals pass by simple majority; (2) an ordinary majority may not remove the listed equal rights from a group.
Rules.
A decision must satisfy both the voting procedure and the higher rights constraint. Passing a vote is not sufficient if the content violates a protected right.
Task.
Did the proposal receive a majority? May it take effect under the stated constitution?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Vote check: 14>5, so the proposal has a simple majority. 2. Content check: the proposal removes a protected equal right (speak at a peaceful meeting) from a group. 3. The higher rights rule therefore blocks the proposal even though the vote passed.
Answer.
It received a majority, but it may not take effect under the stated rights rule.
Knowledge takeaway.
A majority answers who won a vote; it does not by itself answer whether every possible decision is lawful or fair under higher rules.
Formal model.
Two-stage validity test: procedural predicate AND rights-compliance predicate.
